question:
(a) Explain the effect of increasing the intensity of incident radiation on photoelectric current when the frequency is kept fixed above threshold frequency.
(b) Why does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons remain unchanged in this case?

options.A:
(a) Increasing intensity decreases photoelectric current.
(b) $K_{\max}$ increases because intensity increases photon energy.
options.B:
(a) At fixed frequency above threshold, increasing intensity increases photon number per second and hence photoelectric current.
(b) $K_{\max}=h\nu-\phi_0$ remains unchanged because frequency and work function are unchanged; intensity does not change energy per photon.
options.C:
(a) Photoelectric current remains constant with intensity.
(b) $K_{\max}$ decreases because photons share energy.
options.D:
(a) Both photoelectric current and $K_{\max}$ double with intensity.
(b) The work function doubles.
